category_title: Young students with EBD, ADHD, and ODD exhibiting noncompliance and disrobing behaviors
minimal_context: Axel is sitting in his individual work area being asked to complete a reading assignment by his teacher.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Axel, it is time to work on your reading assignment in your work area.

STUDENT: I don't want to read! It's too hard! (pushes the book away, looking angry)

TUTOR: You need to open the book and start reading the first page.

STUDENT: No! I'm not doing it! (kicks off his shoes)

TUTOR: Please put your shoes back on and look at your book.

STUDENT: (Screams a swear word, pulls off his socks, makes an obscene gesture, and throws the book out of the work area)

options.A: Review the consequence maps every morning before the first work session. Give the student the clipboard containing the maps and calm down schedule, letting him decide which to review first. Read the negative behaviors and consequences first, followed by the positive ones.
options.B: Ask the student how he learns best during academic work sessions, and provide more focused one-on-one attention while he is in his individual work area completing the reading assignment.
options.C: Provide extra time to complete the reading assignments, offering flexibility with timelines during the academic work sessions in the individual work area before moving on to the next scheduled activity.
options.D: Gradually fade support during the reading assignments and transfer responsibility to the student over time, stepping back during the academic work sessions in the individual work area.
